title: Point-dependent designs and the square-root barrier of the ETH-refutation method
objective: Decide, within declared limits, whether point-dependent swap designs can beat the square root in the exponent of the openai/math family 378 counting method: construct and exactly verify cube-polynomial families CP(Q,R) with per-direction bad fraction at most R^-C, C > 4, at Q about R^((C+2)/3), or prove a lower bound beta*(Q,R) >= R^-O(1) for Q >= R^(2+delta) for all families or for a precisely defined natural subclass, preserving every exact counterexample and partial bound.
deliverables: A survey note on the closest work (Turan problems in the hypercube, probabilistic and threshold degree of parity, rigidity of direction networks) with reading-list entries and inspection levels
Construction track: explicit families for CP(Q,R) at ratios Q/R >= R, each re-verified in exact rational arithmetic, with a table against the slab and window families

Lower-bound track: a proved bound for a precisely defined class of designs (for example region-based designs built from global formulas), or for all designs at R = 2 with generic nodes, with the exact step that fails for general families
Lean statements and proofs for every new design lemma used in a claimed exponent change, added to problems/eth/lean with a regenerated verification.json
A separate critic's verdict on every claimed theorem, and an updated RANKING.md and novelty ledger
success_criteria: Every claimed family is exactly verified; floating-point or modular evidence alone is reported as empirical

No improvement of the exponent is claimed unless the design lemma is Lean-checked, the cost accounting is re-derived from the preprint's display (2.9) and constraints, and a distinct critic accepts it
A lower bound states exactly which class of designs it covers; method-level barriers are not presented as barriers for all algorithms
Negative results, failed constructions and counterexamples to conjectures are preserved in the problem files
stop_conditions: Two proposal/review rounds are exhausted; record the strongest surviving statements and the open obligation
Exact computations exceed about 4 CPU hours in total or 16 GiB of memory
A claimed construction fails exact verification twice after repair; preserve it as a counterexample to the heuristic
The upstream working group reports an error in the parts of the preprint the cost model uses; re-scope before continuing
No paid provider calls, publication or external contact beyond the user-authorized repository work
